title: SASSA Old Age Grant 2026: Amount
description: SASSA Older Persons (old age) grant 2026: amount, income and asset limits, documents, online application and confirmed payment dates.
author: Lucky Cungwa

sections.title: What is the SASSA Older Persons Grant?
sections.content: The SASSA Older Persons Grant, commonly called the Old Age Pension, is a monthly payment from the South African government to citizens and permanent residents aged 60 and older. It is the most widely accessed permanent grant in South Africa, supporting millions of seniors who are no longer in formal employment. The grant is means-tested, meaning your income and assets must be below a certain threshold to qualify. As of 2026, the grant amounts are {{old_age_pension_amount_under75}} per month for beneficiaries under 75 and {{old_age_pension_amount_over75}} per month for those aged 75 and older.

sections.title: SASSA Old Age Grant 2026: Quick Answer
sections.content:
SASSA old age grant 2026: the Older Persons Grant pays {{old_age_pension_amount_under75}} a month for beneficiaries under 75 and {{old_age_pension_amount_over75}} for those 75 and older. You can apply online at services.sassa.gov.za or at a SASSA office. You need your 13-digit ID, proof of income (or an affidavit), proof of residence, proof of marital status and proof of assets. The grant is means-tested. SASSA does not publish a guaranteed processing time, so apply as early as you can and keep your receipt.

Next payment: the November 2026 Older Persons payment is Friday 30 October 2026, brought forward because of the 4 November Local Government Elections public holiday. The December payment is Wednesday 2 December 2026. See the November 2026 schedule.

sections.title: Eligibility Requirements
sections.content:
To qualify for the SASSA Older Persons Grant in 2026, you must meet all the following requirements:
  • Age: You must be 60 years or older.
  • Citizenship or residency: You must be a South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee.
  • Income threshold: Your income must not exceed {{old_age_income_threshold_single}} per month if single, or {{old_age_income_threshold_married}} combined if married.
  • Asset threshold: Your assets must not exceed {{old_age_asset_threshold_single}} for a single person or {{old_age_asset_threshold_married}} for a married couple. The value of your primary home is excluded.
  • Not receiving another grant: You cannot receive another social grant for yourself, though you may receive the Grant-in-Aid as a top-up.
  • Not in state care: You must not be living in a state-funded institution.

sections.title: Required Documents
sections.content:
You need the following to apply for the Older Persons Grant:
  • 13-digit bar-coded ID (green ID book or smart ID card)
  • Proof of income — pension slip, bank statements (last 3 months), or an affidavit if you have no income
  • Proof of marital status — marriage certificate, divorce decree, or spousal death certificate if applicable
  • Proof of residence — utility bill or affidavit confirming your address
  • Proof of assets — property valuations, investment statements

steps.title: Start Your Application (Online or In Person)
steps.content: You can now start your Older Persons Grant application online via the official SASSA Services Portal at services.sassa.gov.za. Register an account, log in, and complete the online application for the Older Persons Grant. Alternatively, you can apply in person at your nearest SASSA office. Find your nearest office on our resources page.

steps.title: Bring All Required Documents
steps.content: Take your ID, proof of income, proof of residence, and any other supporting documents to the office.

steps.title: Complete the Application Form
steps.content: A SASSA official will help you fill out the application form. Make sure all information is accurate and matches your ID document.

steps.title: Receive Your Receipt
steps.content: After submitting, you will receive a receipt with a reference number. Keep this safe — it is your proof of application.

steps.title: Wait for Processing
steps.content: SASSA will process your application and conduct a means test. This usually takes between 30 and 90 days. You can check your application status at the same SASSA office.

sections.title: Grant Amounts & 2026 Payment Dates
sections.content:
The Older Persons Grant amounts for 2026 are:
  • Under 75 years: {{old_age_pension_amount_under75}} per month
  • 75 years and older: {{old_age_pension_amount_over75}} per month
  • Grant-in-Aid top-up: If you need full-time care, you may qualify for an additional {{grant_in_aid_amount}} per month through the Grant-in-Aid
Payments are made on the first few working days of each month. In October 2026, the Older Persons Grant was paid on Friday, 2 October, and the next Older Persons payment is Friday, 30 October 2026 (the November cycle, brought forward ahead of the 4 November Local Government Elections public holiday) — both confirmed by SASSA. See the October 2026 schedule, the November 2026 schedule and the full payment calendar.

sections.title: Collection Methods
sections.content:
You can collect your Older Persons Grant through:
  • Bank transfer — paid directly into your bank account
  • Postbank Black Card — the replacement for the phased-out SASSA Gold Card, which stopped working on 31 August 2026. Get your free Black Card at Shoprite, Checkers, Usave, Pick n Pay, Boxer or Spar and your balance carries over automatically
  • Retail collection — collect at Pick n Pay, Boxer, Shoprite, Checkers, or USave
  • Home delivery — available for beneficiaries who are unable to travel due to illness or disability
You do not need to withdraw your money on the first day. Your grant is safe in your account until you need it.

faqs.q: Can I work and still receive the Old Age Pension?
faqs.a: Yes, but your total monthly income must stay below the means test threshold. If you earn a pension from a former employer, SASSA will deduct this from your grant amount.
Your grant automatically increases to the higher amount for beneficiaries over 75. You do not need to reapply.

faqs.q: Can I apply before I turn 60?
faqs.a: No, you must have reached your 60th birthday to qualify. You should apply as soon as possible after your birthday.

faqs.q: Can I apply for the Old Age Grant online?
faqs.a: Yes. You can start your application online via the official SASSA Services Portal at services.sassa.gov.za. Register an account, log in, and complete the online application. You may still be asked to visit a SASSA office to submit physical documents like your ID and proof of residence.

faqs.q: What if I am too frail to visit a SASSA office?
faqs.a: You can authorize a family member to apply on your behalf. They must bring a letter of authorization, your ID, and their own ID.

faqs.q: How much is the SASSA old age grant in 2026?
faqs.a: The Older Persons Grant pays {{old_age_pension_amount_under75}} a month for beneficiaries under 75 and {{old_age_pension_amount_over75}} a month for those aged 75 and older. If you need full-time care, you may also qualify for the Grant-in-Aid top-up.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the SASSA old age grant online?
faqs.a: Start at services.sassa.gov.za, the official SASSA Services Portal. Register an account, log in, and complete the Older Persons Grant application. You may still be asked to visit a SASSA office to submit original documents or complete a biometric check. Applications are free.

faqs.q: When is the old age grant paid in November 2026?
faqs.a: The November 2026 Older Persons payment is Friday 30 October 2026. SASSA brought the cycle forward because 4 November 2026 is the Local Government Elections public holiday. The next Older Persons payment after that is Wednesday 2 December 2026.

faqs.q: What is the income threshold for the SASSA old age grant?
faqs.a: For 2026, the income threshold is {{old_age_income_threshold_single}} a month for a single person and {{old_age_income_threshold_married}} combined for a married couple. Your assets must not exceed {{old_age_asset_threshold_single}} for a single person or {{old_age_asset_threshold_married}} for a married couple. The value of your primary home is excluded.

faqs.q: Can I receive the old age grant and a private pension?
faqs.a: Yes, but your private pension counts as income in the means test. If your total income is above the threshold, you may not qualify or you may receive a reduced grant. Declare the pension when you apply and when your income changes.

faqs.q: What happens if my old age grant is under review?
faqs.a: A review is an administrative check that you still qualify. It is not an automatic cancellation. Attend the appointment or respond within the deadline with your ID, proof of income and any documents SASSA asks for. If you ignore it, the grant can be suspended. See our SASSA grant review and verification guide for the full process.

faqs.q: How do I check my SASSA old age grant status?
faqs.a: Old age grant applications are not checked on the SRD portal. Use the reference number on your application receipt, visit the SASSA office where you applied, or call 0800 60 10 11. Ask for the specific status of your Older Persons Grant application.
